facts.text: Santa Cruz de la Cañada was founded April 22, 1695 by Governor Diego de Vargas as New Mexico's second formal municipality.
The town's original name, Villa Nueva de Santa Cruz de los Españoles Mejicanos del Rey Nuestro Señor Carlos Segundo, honored King Charles II.
Nestled 25 miles northwest of Santa Fe, Santa Cruz sits half‑mile east of Española at 5,655 ft above sea level in the Santa Cruz River valley.
The current Santa Cruz Catholic Church, built 1733‑1748, replaced an earlier structure that had begun to collapse.
In the early 20th century, mechanized farming and improved transportation began reshaping Santa Cruz's irrigation‑driven agriculture along the Santa Cruz River.
The 1837 Revolt, centered in Santa Cruz de la Cañada, marked a pivotal uprising against Mexican governor Albino Pérez.
